## Agentic Systems Notation {#sec-notation-agentic}

Agentic systems introduce a third layer of systems notation for multi-turn trajectories, closed-loop control, memory hierarchies, and compounding reliability. Some symbols below are reserved for trajectory traces, verification signals, and tokenomics; defining them centrally keeps the canonical form unambiguous across the chapters. The central formulation is the **Agentic Trajectory Law**:

$$\tau = \big( (a_0, o_1, v_1), (a_1, o_2, v_2), \dots, (a_{N-1}, o_N, v_N) \big)$$

accompanied by the **Trajectory Goodput Law**:

$$\mathcal{G} = \frac{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{success}}} T_i}{\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{all}}} T_j}$$

and the **Compounding Reliability Bound**:

$$P_{\text{success}} \le \prod_{i=1}^N p_i \le p^N$$

### Agent trajectories and closed-loop control {#sec-notation-trajectories}

The closed-loop trajectory formalizes the execution trace of an agent interacting with external tools, environments, and verification oracles.

| **Symbol**       | **Definition**                     | **Unit**       | **Notes**                                                                                                        |
|:-----------------|:-----------------------------------|:---------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\tau$**       | **Agentic Trajectory**             | Tuple          | Ordered sequence of action proposals, observations, and verification signals over horizon $N$.                   |
| **$a_t$**        | **Action Proposal**                | Token sequence | Action emitted by the neural policy $\pi_\theta$ at turn $t$ (internal deliberation or external tool call).      |
| **$o_t$**        | **Environment Observation**        | String/Bytes   | Output payload returned across the sandbox boundary from tool execution or external feedback at turn $t$.        |
| **$v_t$**        | **Verification Signal**            | Boolean/Score  | Evaluation outcome from runtime verification oracle at turn $t$ gating state commitment.                         |
| **$s_t$**        | **Ground-Truth Environment State** | State record   | Physical or digital state of external environment (filesystem, database, process table) at turn $t$.             |
| **$h_t$**        | **Working Context Buffer**         | Token sequence | Active context window assembled from system instructions, trajectory history, and observations at turn $t$.      |
| **$\pi_\theta$** | **Neural Policy**                  | Distribution   | Stochastic autoregressive foundation model parameterized by weights $\theta$.                                    |
| **$\text{ACB}$** | **Agent Control Block**            | Struct         | In-memory OS-level descriptor tracking trajectory lineage, KV page tables, capability leases, and watchdog caps. |

### The H-S-A-C systems taxonomy {#sec-notation-hsac}

The H-S-A-C coordinate space classifies autonomous workloads across four orthogonal axes of systems complexity and operational risk.

| **Symbol** | **Definition**          | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                       |
|:-----------|:------------------------|:--------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$H$**    | **Operational Horizon** | Turns         | Trajectory turn depth; sequential actions required to satisfy the delegated objective ($H=1$ to $1{,}000+$).    |
| **$S$**    | **State Complexity**    | Discrete rank | Scope of tracked mutable state: in-context buffer, external local filesystem, or distributed multi-service DB.  |
| **$A$**    | **Authority Level**     | Discrete rank | Effector blast radius: $A_0$ (read-only advisory), $A_1$ (sandboxed), $A_2$ (reversible), $A_3$ (irreversible). |
| **$C$**    | **Invariant Closure**   | Discrete rank | Verification rigor: open heuristic/human review vs. closed deterministic unit tests, compilers, or proofs.      |

### Silicon physics, memory, and latency walls {#sec-notation-physics-walls}

Agentic workloads alternate between compute-bound prompt prefill, memory-bandwidth-bound token decode, and I/O-bound tool waits.

| **Symbol**               | **Definition**                     | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                    |
|:-------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:--------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$p$**                  | **Single-Step Action Accuracy**    | Probability   | Probability that the policy selects a correct, non-divergent action at an isolated turn ($p \in [0, 1]$).    |
| **$N$**                  | **Trajectory Horizon Depth**       | Integer       | Total sequential turns in a trajectory. *(Not device count; context disambiguates).*                         |
| **$P_{\text{success}}$** | **Trajectory Success Probability** | Probability   | Probability of completing an $N$-step trajectory without unrecovered failure ($P_{\text{success}} \le p^N$). |
| **$T_{\text{active}}$**  | **Active Attention Working Set**   | Tokens        | Working set of tokens actively participating in self-attention at turn $t$.                                  |
| **$M_{\text{KV}}$**      | **Key-Value Cache Memory**         | bytes (GB)    | Accelerator HBM footprint dedicated to storing cached keys and values across the context sequence.           |
| **$T_{\text{prefill}}$** | **Prefill Latency**                | seconds       | Compute-bound wall-clock time to process prompt tokens in parallel via GEMM kernels.                         |
| **$T_{\text{decode}}$**  | **Per-Token Decode Latency**       | seconds/token | Memory-bandwidth-bound wall-clock time to generate an autoregressive token via GEMV kernels.                 |
| **$T_{\text{tool}}$**    | **Tool Execution Latency**         | seconds       | Wall-clock time spent waiting for external compilers, test suites, or network I/O (Tool-Wait memory tax).    |
| **$\mathcal{O}(T^2)$**   | **Quadratic Attention Scaling**    | FLOPs         | Algorithmic complexity of standard full self-attention over sequence length $T$.                             |

### Macro-efficiency and tokenomics {#sec-notation-tokenomics}

Macro-efficiency measures end-to-end task completion economics rather than isolated token throughput.

| **Symbol**             | **Definition**                 | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                   |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------|:--------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\mathcal{G}$**      | **Trajectory Goodput**         | Dimensionless | Fraction of allocated compute time or FLOPs spent on trajectories reaching verified completion ($[0, 1]$).  |
| **$J_{\text{task}}$**  | **Energy per Resolved Task**   | Joules/task   | Cumulative electrical energy consumed across prefill, decode, and tool sandboxes per successful outcome.    |
| **$C_{\text{task}}$**  | **Cost per Resolved Task**     | \$/task       | Cumulative financial expenditure (inference tokens + leased infrastructure) per successful outcome.         |
| **$\text{TAF}$**       | **Token Amplification Factor** | Dimensionless | Ratio of total tokens generated across an agent fleet to initial user prompt tokens ($\text{TAF} \ge 1.0$). |
| **$B_{\text{token}}$** | **Token Budget Ceiling**       | Tokens        | Watchdog limit on maximum tokens allocated to a trajectory before preemption or termination.                |
| **$B_{\text{cost}}$**  | **Financial Budget Ceiling**   | \$            | Hard monetary expenditure ceiling enforced by admission control before trajectory termination.              |

### Additional collision points {#sec-notation-agentic-collisions}

The agentic systems context introduces symbol collisions across classical ML and distributed systems notation:

| **Symbol** | **ML Meaning (Vol 1)** | **Distributed Meaning (Vol 2)** | **Agentic Meaning (Vol 3)** | **Our Convention**                                                                                                                                   |
|:-----------|:-----------------------|:--------------------------------|:----------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| $\tau$     | Drift threshold        | Checkpoint interval             | Agentic trajectory trace    | **Context-dependent**. In this book, bare $\tau$ denotes the trajectory tuple. Checkpoint intervals use $\tau_{\text{ckpt}}$ or $\tau_{\text{opt}}$. |
| $H$        | Shannon entropy        | Hardware host nodes             | Operational horizon depth   | **Context-dependent**. $H$ denotes sequential horizon depth in H-S-A-C. Shannon entropy uses $\mathcal{H}$.                                          |
| $N$        | Dataset size           | Accelerator device count        | Trajectory turn count       | **Context-dependent**. In trajectory probability bounds, $N$ denotes turns. Fleet device count uses $N_{\text{total}}$ or $N_{\text{dev}}$.          |
| $a$        | Activation value       | Acceleration / scaling factor   | Action proposal             | **Subscripted**. $a_t$ represents the action proposal at step $t$; learning rate uses $\eta$ or $\alpha$.                                            |
| $s$        | Sequence length        | Seconds (time unit)             | Environment state           | **Context-dependent**. Subscripted $s_t$ denotes environment state; sequence length uses $T$; seconds unit is written as $\text{s}$.                 |
| $C$        | Compute FLOPs          | Channel capacity                | Invariant closure           | **Context-dependent**. In H-S-A-C, $C$ denotes closure rank. Compute budget uses $C_{\text{compute}}$, financial cost uses $C_{\text{task}}$.        |

### Additional units {#sec-notation-agentic-units}

*   **Trajectory Goodput ($\mathcal{G}$)**: Reported as a percentage or fraction in $[0, 1]$. In contrast to raw token throughput ($\text{tokens/s}$), goodput accounts only for tokens emitted within trajectories that satisfy verified termination invariants.
*   **Unit economics**: Financial cost is reported in US dollars per resolved task ($\$/\text{task}$); energy efficiency is reported in Joules per resolved task ($J/\text{task}$) or kilowatt-hours per resolved task ($\text{kWh}/\text{task}$).
*   **Token volume and velocity**: Context capacities and cumulative consumption use $\text{kTok}$ ($10^3$ tokens) and $\text{MTok}$ ($10^6$ tokens); serving throughput uses $\text{tokens/s}$.
